text:
After 923 games as an Islander, Anders Lee is wearing a different sweater at 36, and the early returns are better than the box score. Three goals in 21 games looks like a slow start. Our numbers say his chances add up to 6.3 expected goals (the quality of his looks), so the finish is what's missing, not the work. Utah takes 62.5% of the expected goals at five on five when he's on the ice in his 14 minutes a night.

That fits who he has been. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 99th percentile among forwards for driving chances last season, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking put him in the 91st percentile for scoring chances from the area right in front of the net. One wrinkle worth watching: 20% of his setups come from behind the net, against 8% for a typical forward. The cold stretch has dragged on (one goal in his last ten games), but the net-front work hasn't changed, and that's usually where a player like this gets paid back.
